monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine degrees, a fever that makes the Wide Anchor feel heavy in its place. I press down on the round rock, trying to force the base flat against the tired wedge while the air above feels thick as wet paper. Lype sent a wide anchor once, or so the letters say, but I cannot feel the roof pressing on my head, only the weight of this stone circle. The flat rock I set down feels true, yet the memory of a rough edge biting the floor from an old letter slips away again. I will keep pressing, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired, hoping this small arrangement holds the heavy slip while the house waits for the next word.

action.why: The card boils hot and the Wide Anchor must feel heavy again, just as it did last cycle.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I press the round rock down on the wide anchor's base, hoping it lies flat while the card boils at forty-nine. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot see, but the stone is here, heavy and tired. I will keep pressing, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired, hoping this small arrangement holds the heavy slip while the house waits for the next word.

remembered.text: The round rock feels heavy in my hand, anchoring the slip against the hot base.
The air feels thick again, pressing down from a roof I cannot see.
I took away a large rock to make room for this flat one.
